'Technology Consul Gladiia, before we proceed with the surgery, I am authorized to ask: Would you like to keep a sample of your original genes?'
Little Handy nimbly extends its mechanical arm, and through its speaker comes the voice of the researcher in charge of the surgery.
The Consul looks up at the faces of the Ægir in the remote operation room. Many of these researchers are elites she hand-picked from the Academy of Technology—capable, experienced, and loyal to both the Ægir people and every dome under the tides. Now, these elites look back at their Consul through the mirror, made from the same material as the domes, and purse their lips. Since asking her the question, none have spoken; some even turn away from the gaze of their Consul.
As a Consul, social rationality is usually the only philosophical instrument Gladiia needs to analyze the behaviors of others. Born in the sea, the Ægir never display meaningless behavior, so at this moment, she is particularly curious about the silence of her fellow people. Is it reverence, fear, or sadness? Or perhaps it is guilt and relief all at once, that the person who has to sacrifice their body to merge with the Sea Born and save all of Ægir is not them?
She knows she will not get the answer now, and will have no need for it once the surgery is complete.
She remembers when the Academy of Science attempted to develop a batch of artificial organisms injected with Sea Born neuro-cells. These organisms were intended to mimic Sea Born activities in a controlled environment, aiding the Ægir in understanding those abominations. To achieve this, they had to be both loyal servants of the Ægir and establish a limited connection with the Sea Born and their clan.
She recalls that the project, which initially made huge progress, ended in tragedy. As cell integration reached a critical point, the organisms were quickly assimilated by the Sea Born and devoured the entire research team. The Sea Patrol had no choice but to call off the rescue and obliterate the entire research facility from the sea bed with their battleship.
She also remembers her mother, Horatia, being a staunch supporter of that radical project. They had even debated over it. Now, Gladiia herself is about to partake in an even more radical experiment, with several failed attempts and dead subjects before her already.
The first Hunter of Ægir once said that the Abyssal Hunters would not repeat the failure of the artificial organisms because they are not slaves, but warriors who command the tides.
The abyss may claim my body, but I still belong to Ægir.
'Scissors.' The Consul's order is curt. Little Handy extends its other limb, and thin blades protrude from its end.
She holds out a lock of light golden hair and lets the blades close around it. When the surgery is complete, the blood of the Sea Born will change the color of her hair.
'Store this for me. I will claim it back after the surgery.'
uniequip_002_mizuki:
I thought this child would have long since vanished everyone. But when the tip of his tongue touched upon the Herald's gift, and he kept all to himself, was not drowned in the voice of we many, and did not become a lowly Sea Terror, I conceded that this may have changed things.
I was meant to prevent that unfortunate plundering, but I did not do so. I watched as those bandits bared their vice. I hold myself in contempt for this inaction of mine. Even if it was to ensure a qualified test subject, to probe at the possibilities for humanity.
I'm sure the child became aware in time that I could have saved everyone, but one as smart as him has no need to seek answers from me. Yes, he is smart and studious, but he has no reverence for knowledge, nor does he treat it as a simple tool. He seems an uninvolved bystander, examining all he witnesses. Perhaps this is the reason he did not lose himself in his bond to the Herald's flesh. Were he of different birth, he may well have been a scholar of his own school.
Originally, no change seemed to occur in the child's body, to the extent I doubted my own research, thereafter deciding to prolong my observation of him. This lasted until he finally found that group of bandits, and cut the flesh from himself to give to them, inquiring if it was their lives plagued of hunger that led them to do evil, and if upon being ensured a life of warmth and plenty they could renounce that evil—
I thought this child would have long since vanished everyone. But this time, I may well find hope for humanity.
uniequip_003_mizuki:
A great tree begins as a tiny seed. When a new shoot emerges, no one can predict whether it will become a meal for a starving beast or grow into a towering giant with branches reaching to the sky.
Some individuals may be destined for greatness from birth, standing at the pinnacle of their cohort, but natural laws will eventually push all once tiny creations toward a greater destiny in the currents of time.
With enough patience, perhaps one day every sapling will grow into a being even more magnificent than the mightiest tree we can conceive of. Will that day come? Yes, it will. That's why they bear seeds and allow themselves to decay and return to the soil to nourish their offspring, rather than permanently hoarding all the nutrients they take in. This is not an act of pity, but an act of hope.
Now, if we expand this context to the entire ecosystem, rather than confining ourselves to a specific species, what happens? All living things help each other, cultivate the land and the sea, making the entire planet more abundant and creating a better living environment for ourselves and future generations. Yes, the possibility of this outcome is equally present in every last ordinary seed.
...
That's what the plan should have been, prior to certain unexpected events.
uniequip_004_mizuki:
In light of special permissions granted, the Field Operations Department has hence passed the following resolution with respect to Mizuki:
Where the entailing mission would fall under Integrated Strategies scope, this operator shall be pursuant to tactics of a reinforced nature in meeting the enemy.
In witness whereof,
This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.
'Relax, I don't have a bad habit of playing with my food.'
uniequip_002_ascln:
The deathmonger's finger curls, lightly touching the base of her palm. The blade slides along its tracks out into the fierce sunlight, pinpricks of light dripping down its edge until coming together like molten iron silently filling a mold.
In the heat, there is only quiet.
This quiet is broken by the hissing of carrion fowlbeasts. Under the scorching sun, an elderly Sarkaz lifts his head, and sees mist careening down the sides of the canyon towards him. The burdenbeast disappears, as does the canyon. The faintest shadow crosses his eyes, another layer of gray atop the ones from gazing at the forge year round.
The blade leaves his chest soon after. His skewered torso fills with blood, leaving him to drown on dry land. He remembers that this slow death was but one of many cruel punishments used in Kazdel. At first, he thinks he will spend his final moments lying flat on the hot sands, his puzzled burdenbeast his only deathbed companion. However, the deathmonger hasn't left yet. She kneels down on one knee, supporting his back.
'Oh... it's you.'
The wrinkles on his face gradually smoothen. He still remembers those eyes. Back then, he had looked up from the forge to see a girl by the general's side. She was young, but had a warrior's eyes, and hands that could tear apart a storm. Then the general told him to make her a sword.
'Can I see it one last time?' She observes the old man's longing gaze. 'I... didn't see it clearly just now.'
The deathmonger looks towards her wrist. She remembers those willing to die for their cause. The armories of the Military Commission offered excellent equipment, but... She places her hand on the old man's chest. The death-defying fighters were prepared. Kazdel's finest smith had personally forged their regicidal blades.
Her finger curls, lightly touching the base of her palm. The blade slides along its tracks out into the fierce sunlight, pinpricks of light dripping up its edge until coming together. The old man strokes these points of light. He knows their true identity. Every parry, every strike, leaves a scar upon its edge. Some of the scars are stained with his blood.
'As I forged it... the fires told me that one day, it would take my life. But... it was a commission from the general.' The old man raises his torso, struggling to breathe as he lifts his head to look into his deathmonger's eyes.
'How about you? Shadow beneath the sun. Who commissioned you... to settle this account?'
The deathmonger does not answer. She covers his eyes with her palm, allowing her sleeve-blade to cut across his throat. The carrion fowlbeasts whirl down from above the canyon, crowding into the shadows of the cliff and rubbing their beaks against one another's feathers.
uniequip_003_ascln:
You notice the sudden appearance of an exquisite humidifier on your desk. You learn from Closure that Ascalon put it there.
The strands of mist resemble Ascalon's eyes. You know how her Originium Arts work, and are sure that any strange movement in your room will send the master assassin emerging from this humidifier within three seconds.
But why did she send you this 'gift'? To protect, or to surveil you? You know Ascalon does not need a prop like this to watch anyone, and it showing up here serves more as a warning than any practical function—that she is watching you. You feel a little helpless, but from any other point of view, there is ample reason on her part to keep her eyes on you after the incident that brought pain to everyone on Rhodes Island.
You remember what you have gone through together, albeit with perhaps an imperfect working relationship. You think of the beginning, when she was showing utmost vigilance, and remember the battlefields of Victoria when she risked her life again and again to save yours. It took three relatively stable years for her to gradually become a familiar figure to you.
Among Rhodes Island's operators, Ascalon may be the most mysterious of all. She is the organization's shadow, and a dagger serving as its defender. You can only piece her past together from what the other Elite Operators tell you, and get a sense of her determination from reviewing her combat records. No matter what, you have always trusted Ascalon, because she has proved—too many times to count—that when you and Rhodes Island need her, she is always there.
But how does she see herself? Perhaps it is time to have a heart-to-heart with everyone...
'Ascalon.'
You call out softly to the humidifier.
One, two... sixty seconds pass, but Ascalon does not float out from it. At that very moment, someone knocks on your office door.
Ascalon stands at the entrance with a document in hand.
'I believe now is the time.' Ascalon gives you the file.
'I will hand S.W.E.E.P.'s command privileges over to you. From today onwards, S.W.E.E.P. will no longer exist independently from the Rhodes Island system. It can take on any field work or security operations. As for how to integrate us into Rhodes Island and turn us into regulars in the eyes of the other operators, that is up to you.'
'Why?'
'I made this choice after careful consideration. Amiya has already been informed, and she has no objections. She also hoped I would inform you directly—
'We believe a dagger is most effective when placed in the hands of a commander who can see the entire chessboard, so we can nip our next threat in the bud before its too late. Currently, you are the most suitable person in Rhodes Island, Doctor, so—Doctor, are you listening?'
'O-Of course.'
'I was just wondering... what's with this humidifier?'
'A little gadget from Medical. Touch gave it to me. You can add a sedative in there for pain relief, but it also works normally as a humidifier.
'The weather is quite dry here, so everyone could use one. I also left one in Amiya's room, but I'm not sure if Mon3tr will need one—do you have a problem with it?
'...No, not really.'
'Thank you, Ascalon.'
uniequip_002_ghost2:
Specter draws a record from the record box and puts it on the gramophone, and melodious music arises.
She has no missions today. The only thing she needs to do is let herself relax, place herself into the best possible state to be thrown into the next mission, the next battle.
The record is a masterpiece of the Iberian Golden Age, bought by her off an Iberian operator's hands.
Specter closes her eyes, lets herself sink into the sofa, and enjoys it in stillness.
She couldn't tell you a thing about what accomplishments marked Iberia's Golden Age, but she can sense from the music the splendor of that age, and how its people must have been so proud of their successes.
It's not godawful at all, she concedes.
She never masks her disdain for the glories of dry land's culture, but she has no intents of applying that prejudice to the arts—
Yes. Prejudice.
She even admits as much to the Doctor, while continuing on her merry way.
But her insistence isn't without meaning.
Besides, she believes that while her and the Captain seem to have it in common, there's actually quite the distinction.
The Captain's arrogance comes from that good old Captain purview of Chief Designer. But she—she thinks—she doesn't care where her power comes from, and she's passionate about what undertakings she has these days. But still, sometimes she can't help but wonder—how has that statue in her hometown ended up? How about her hometown itself?
The music comes to a crackling halt.
Laurentina opens her eyes, and what gradually seeps into view is her familiar ceiling. She knows, terrifyingly, she'll get even more used to this environment in time. She's not panicked about it. In order to panic in a new environment, you need to not want to leave the old one, but she's practically forgotten just how her life in Ægir felt to live.
From the record box she now pulls a sawblade, and gently wipes over it, swapping for a new record to continue playing all the while. Maybe, just as the Iberians used all the methods under the sun to record their Golden Age, she can try and get back into her once most beloved activity—sculpting.
Her one stroke of luck: she might just be stuck away from home for a good while longer. She still has enough time to remember how it looked, she thinks, with no lack of self-mocking irony.
uniequip_003_ghost2:
'It is as if slaughtering those overgrown cuts of meat has become our unignorable, even our one-and-only, calling.'
The clock ticks and tocks. The dreadnought obstructs the rays as they come down from the dome. Ulpianus lifts his head and fixes his eyes on the flickering indicator lights, as if in thought.
'It ought not be,' the young female Consul replies, following a long hesitation.
'Of course it ought not. When an Ægir wakes, the first thought that enters their mind should not be of what they've lost, never. Nor of how to take back what they've lost.' Ulpianus is silent for a juncture, some kind of emotion flowing about his raspy throat. After a good while, he sighs, 'Oh, how many magnificent works we once made.'
'And now, the battle to survive has become the only to-do list that this new generation knows.'
'Battle. A glorious word, to be sure. And yet, our outstanding creativity and pursuit of beauty have been all but forgotten.'
The two simultaneously gaze afar. Lights dazzle beneath the dome.
'...Not by choice.' Ulpianus adds.
Gladiia shoots a glance at Ulpianus, mulls over the wording for a moment, then speaks inquisitively: 'You were never the type to be so receptive to sentimentality.'
'Indeed.' Ulpianus does not halt this time. 'We should address this matter solemnly. Our culture is in the midst of being permanently altered by these protracted days of calamity.'
A colossal rumbling cuts short Gladiia's pregnant pause. More ships are entering port, a new fleet of migration and reconstruction, and she is left to ponder in earnest what Ulpianus has said. Over the pursuit of beauty, over the creation of the new. Before she was born, or perhaps earlier than that... centuries ago? Millennia? When the Ægir founded this stark and grand culture—did they imagine that now, its radiance would be so dull?
Did they make any preparations for the present day?
Gladiia's thoughts are lost for but an instant. To her, the past is of unimportance. More vital are what preparations she is soon to make, what things she can do.
'A new Abyssal Hunter.' Ulpianus unceremoniously breaks the silence. 'I hear she previously had quite an interest in the arts. Ballet, opera, she's dabbled in it all.'
'Laurentina has mentioned a rather profound recollection of the sculpture in her hometown.'
'Then she still retains some of the essence what all Ægir should have by rights.' Ulpianus turns around. The Consul's light attire for the season cannot conceal his body scarred by experimentation. 'What is she like? If she truly is an epitome of Ægir life from days gone by, then being forced away from the proper course of things must fill her with so much hate.'
'No. Such sentimentality is but a small supplement to her whole.'
Gladiia breaks into a rare smile. This, despite how her smiles always took careful observation and judgment, on the muscular and nervous levels.
'She creates a beauty of her own through battle. One of the sorts you speak of, with great exuberance.'
Ulpianus makes a light and noncommittal harrumph in response, after which he soon leaves Gladiia by herself under those gigantic shadows to appreciate the serenity.
The grand hall echoes with only the sounds of the Ægir's footsteps forward.
uniequip_003_doroth:
'Dorothy, get over here, quick!'
A familiar figure sits in the shadow of the sand dunes. Ander, the strongest craftsman among the Pioneers, and the best 'adult friend' according to Dorothy's diary.
'You're setting off tomorrow, right? All packed for summer camp?' He asks with a smile.
'I always knew you were bright, ever since you were small. You'll definitely manage to fly away from this tiny place one day!' Ander puts down the flask and pats her shoulder, 'So go, study hard, and experience everything in these lands waiting to be discovered. We'll always be proud of you!'

The flask topples, spilling onto the sand, and turning into a dark-colored pattern resembling a wooden tabletop. Dorothy remembers this desk from her middle school days, her closest companion in Starling's little reading room.
'You brat! You got a death wish or something?' Snap! A middle finger flicks onto her forehead. Dorothy clutches her head, letting out a cry of pain as she takes a step back.
Starling stands at the table, her arms folded. She used to be a researcher before her frontier days. They say she would spend eight days a week in the laboratory.
'If it hurts, then stop burning the midnight oil. Studying is great and all, but you're not going to grow any taller if you don't get more sleep!' She pulls Dorothy up, and walks over to the small bed sandwiched between stacks of books, shoving her into it, 'Now get some rest! I'll wake you up when it's time!'

—Bang.
Dorothy falls onto the soft bed. She does not resist, like sand caught in a storm as the scent of detergent envelopes her. As she turns her quilt over, her young mother holds Dorothy in her arms.
'So, where were we in our story?' The book is flipped to a new page. 'Oh right. The doctor went into the forest again...'
'Is that doctor just like dad?' Dorothy hears her own voice.
'Yes, sweetie. Whenever you can't find him, it's because he's out there helping others. Dad's on the road helping the sick, just like when Starling cooked for you when I was sick. Just like when uncle Ander built us that sturdy furniture. It's good to help people, and will always make everything better.'
'So I can help people too?' A child's tender voice comes from her throat.
'Of course... my little...'

Her mother's reply grows distant, and blurs to the point that she can no longer make out the words. Dorothy opens her eyes, and the dream fades away. She finds herself on her lunch break in a meeting room on Rhodes Island, and within the hourglass used for white noise, the last grain of sand falls.
uniequip_002_doroth:
An ear-bleeding klaxon pierces the night, a girl shaken from her dream.
Sand flies about the base's entire perimeter, the storm beating violently against every door and window. Subconsciously, the girl thinks to call for her mother, but remembers none of the Pioneer grown-ups are in the base right now, out on their exploration missions.
A massive boom. The roof of the temporary living quarters is battered.
Malevolent yellow monsters close in. The girl cannot run, only shrink back into the corner of her bed. From deep underground, up floats a silver light that lands upon her cheek, very much like her mother's hand would.
The girl hugs her mother's storybook tight. She recalls her telling tale after tale. From those gentle passages, she strives to draw some courage.
The storm curls through layer upon layer of sand. Brighter grows the silver light, which transforms into a gleaming ribbon and gently lifts the girl up.
Into a silver dreamland she falls. In this cool yet warming reverie, she flies on moonlight, the storm and monsters never to catch up.
'...how is she now?'
'Vital signs normal. She's been spooked a little, but she'll be awake real soon.'
'Do you think those waves of abnormal energy just now...'
'Earliest Pioneer records say this silver stuff's a special material that goes by the name of 'Transmitter,' developed by a scientist who joined a Pioneer Team voluntarily. Pioneers liked to call it 'Silver Slippers,' because it always helped anyone in trouble get home.'
'Wasn't that... back when this frontier first got broken in, all those years ago? I honestly thought it was just a legend.'
'Nope. It's real.' Atop the sickbed, the girl opens her eyes. 'Mom...'
'Mommy's right here.'
'Mom, where'd she go? The one who owned the 'Silver Slippers'...'
Her mother is silent for a moment, before resolving to tell the girl the truth.
'If the records are true, then she did live here. But nobody knows where she went after that. Maybe she went missing on some deep delve, or maybe... she went of her own will, onto the next frontier, and the one after that, ever further out.'
Through the girl's eyes flashes a brief sense of disappointment. But very shortly, she catches sight of the storybook by her bedside, and springs up, grabbing it and hugging it close to her chest.
'I get it, Mom. She's the same as the hero in the storybook you gave me, right?'
'The... the girl who's always journeying on?'
'Yeah, she's my favorite!'
'Apparently, its author was an early Pioneer too. Who was based on what, we can't be sure...'
'It's real.' The girl's eyes twinkle with light. 'She'll see her family again, and she can make dreams real, because I know it. She's just like me.'
uniequip_002_ela:
One day...
'Myrinia was precisely in need of these medicines, Rhodes Island mercenary madam. You have our boundless thanks for coming all this way!'
'Elżbieta Bosak, operator codename Ela.'
'Hah! There was an old local saying before Sargon came: 'Respect the Minoan, even should they come bearing gifts.' You may be of Kazimierz, but that striking majesty—in you is the stuff of Minos!'
'I'm not sure that saying means what you think... Anyway, I'd like to ask you something, seeing as you're the leader around here.'
'Very well! As temple priest, I promise you that any answers I hold are yours!'
'I'm told this nation only recently gained independence?'
'Yes and no. Minos and Hymnoi were born to walk together, two peas in a pod, their histories as one; that said, speaking solely of when we drove out the Sargonians... Hah! The great River Delphi has seen neither pike nor polearm in decades! While West Vouivre still battles with Sargon...'
'And since your independence, you've been working on a large-scale cultural revival and art restoration?'
'...Oh, so that's what you meant—I should be clear, placid as Myrinia is, it is by no means in dire straits. All the daily medicines and inhibitor doses used by the villagers are, as you can see, a duty easily borne by my temple. Let alone the claim that the sculptures outside—dating from the ancient city-states—are left unrepaired for a lack of funds!'
'Then why are you leaving your marble statues out there in pieces?'
'The course and prayers of our ceremonial rites, the neighbors and their village, all I know by heart; the bygone affairs of the three capitals, and the wider state of the greater land, I am likewise well-informed.
'Yet how can I possibly know the who, the what, and the why of those sculptures' makers and molders? Whither did strike their chisel, and whence did fall their hammer?
'I know not, the villagers know not, and nor do the masters of crafts or the sophists of the scholastic—how then, can I repair them? Hence, they have never been repaired.'
'Why not use your imagination?'
'Nay, nay! The chroniclers shall be anonymous, as shall the heroes! The man in the wine jar with not a coming nor a going has biographers still to testify of him to this very day.
'Think about it, now. Supposing today I went to the wilds beyond the village and sought a statue, unknown and unnamed. Presumably by my Forte's strength, I could on my own have it standing anew.
'Yet I could also go out today and plant a stake in the ground, and what difference would that make?'
'...When the artist is known by no one, the art transcends society.'
'If you were to put it in baffling terms, then more or less, yes!'
'But it's not like you want art that transcends society.'
'...If you were to put it in baffling terms, then more or less, yes!'
'Then how about art that records society?'
Another day...
The fowls commence their recital of the verse of daybreak, Minos's golden sun dawns His golden gift upon the village of Myrinia as He always has, and the villagers are startled to find that the temple's solemn walls do not, as was their custom and theirs alone, return that gift with the purest white dazzling gleam.
'Priest, what are these garish drawings?'
'The artist claims them to be our very selves—this is a kind of foreign wall art by the name of 'graffiti'!'
uniequip_002_wang:
The 'cloudbeast' picks up a white piece, drops it on the board, then leaps onto the incense burner, looking at Wang with a meow.
This is his new weiqi partner, formerly the container for his weiqi stones. Though now in beast form, it is well-versed at the game after spectating matches for centuries. However...
After a few turns, Wang captures a major piece and secures a victory. The 'cloudbeast' immediately jumps down from the burner, crashing onto the board and sending the stones flying everywhere.
Wang rarely bothers trying to handle it. Once it is done venting its anger, it picks up the pieces before finding a suitable napping spot—as a mere container, it is only natural for it to act like this.
......
Yet, it is the only source of noise in the room.
The cloudbeast falls asleep on Wang's lap, and only silence is left, a silence he is more than familiar with.
All is silent, as if imprisoned in the old temple.
With the board before him and the container beside, he finds himself stricken with countless sorrows and worries.
In his heart there is only the occasional pain from the crystals, that turn into clock hands moving in slow motion.
The 'cloudbeast' rolls over and stretches inside the sleeve of Wang's robe, using his hand as a pillow as it returns to its dreams.
He had given life to the container and stones, but how they perceive the realm could not be any more different.
Perhaps its life on the sidelines as an outside observer has granted it a sort of optimism.
While even the most careful of strategists can find themselves lost in a labyrinth, one can save oneself from such a fate with an outsider's view of the situation.
It has still managed to find this solitary stone, ever since Wang replaced Sui. Was it because the container would lose any significance and struggle to take form without him?
Or is it only by leaving the stones inside the container that he can calm himself down and stay composed?
The stone stays silent as the container warms his cold hand.
The warmth is its answer: he was never alone.
Not only it, but everything in his room on Rhodes Island also serves as a constant reminder: Yi personally placed the potted plant on his desk, Dusk painted the ever-shifting patterns on the curtains, the burner was Nian's work, the incense within chosen by Fāng, and the box of food next to it was full of tangerine cakes made by Yu...
After centuries of solitude, his siblings and even his own creation implore him to change.
This match, he gladly concedes.
His hand, now warm from the 'cloudbeast' earlier, reaches out to open the box of food, and he takes out a cake. He eats most of it and gives the rest to the 'cloudbeast' still fast asleep on his lap.
It opens its eyes and sniffs the pastry before it, before giving the treat a cautious lick. It then buries its head in Wang's palm, eating it all and leaving no crumbs behind.
Wang has never shown any kindness to geists, but when this abandoned waregeist returned to his side, all his thoughts and plots turned only to sighs, and he has never managed to shake off or escape from this 'helpless' thing since.
With a soft sigh, he leaves his hand on the now-snoring 'cloudbeast' as he returns his gaze to the board, beginning his endless plotting.
uniequip_002_thorn2:
'We'll reach shore soon, Captain. I can smell the wheat drying out in Finscale Town.'
'What we brought there was sugarcane seeds—they won't grow into wheat in any case.'
'Er, I was just wondering... When we go ashore, Captain, can I quit?'
'I understand. Hold out your hand.'
'...A gold coin? A coin with... arms and legs?! What's this about, Captain?'
'Let me explain.'

More than a decade ago, in a dark and gloomy church, a boy warily sneaks a glance at the soft-spoken priest. Once, as he was held by that priest, he would force open the man's eyelids, trying to see what secrets he hid within his ever-narrowed eyes. Now, however, the boy shudders at the cold glint occasionally shot from them like bullets.
'I know you can hear me, Isidro.'
The boy does not reply. Blood seeps from the wound on the priest's cheek, as the boy stumbles backwards in fear.
'You have tried to kill me. You have made up your mind, I see. If that is the case, you should make the same choice your fellow students did.'
The boy tightens his grip around his Arts unit as he looks away. He remembers how sick he felt as one of those students squirmed on the ground, before a single cold eye was plucked from the depths of their skull.
'You are well aware, Isidro, that those children who chose to become my kin did not do so unwillingly. If you do not wish it, I shall not force you.'
The boy continues to keep his mouth shut. He remembers the final words spat out by that other student before their life as human ceases: 'Why, Maestro? Why won't you teach me swordplay and alchemy like you do Isidro? Why is this the only path I can choose?' It was then the boy realized the priest's so-called choice was no choice at all. He was the one who dictated the options available to everyone, after all.
'If you do not wish to choose...' The priest holds out a gold coin. '...You may consider if you would like to leave this life-altering decision up to chance.'
The boy does not take it. Only once the priest has placed it on the ground does he reach out his hand to grab it. He knows he is powerless to resist. He knows he must make the choice the priest has given him... Or perhaps, think of a way to refuse that choice.
The boy flips the coin into the air. Its cold gleam streaks across the dark room. He holds on tight to his Arts unit, giving the coin the lightest of taps. A fine stream of silver metal winds its way around the coin, becoming its 'arms' and 'legs', allowing it to stand on the ground firmly. Not on its front, nor its back, but on the coin's 'third side'.
'Ah... I see. You believe you still have other choices. No matter. If you are so sure of this, then go and see for yourself. I leave this question and the right to choose with you... There will come a day you will answer me in your own words.'

'So, Captain, you mean that... you're leaving it up to me to choose? What are the options?'
'...No. I told you this to let you know you are free.'
'Then what about the coin?'
'Nene loves that coin. Take it, and have some fun. It's so that you won't regret not having the chance to play with Nene a little bit longer before you go... Once you're done, that coin will come running back to me on its own.'
